acceptance: An agent that reads only `AGENTS.md` and the pages it links can find: why the refusal happens after a subagent writes, the recovery command, and when not to use it.
The refusal message printed by the write preflight names that page, or already prints the takeover command with the same condition; shown by a test of the message.
If option (b) is chosen instead: a test shows a live second session is still refused and a finished same-process subagent is not.
context: 2026-11-16: option (a) delivered in pull request #4253, merged as 52f4db96b3e70443541a63ed3b09bad2507416ad. Option (b) was ruled out: the ownership record holds a session id plus the harness pid and start time, and a finished subagent has the same live pid as a running one, so the check cannot tell them apart. `docs/agent/handoffs.md` (linked from AGENTS.md) has the section 'Taking over a worktree'; the refusal message names that page and the condition; the refusal test requires both. The hosted review found that the first wording left out a successor subagent taking over from a stopped sibling; fixed before merge.
description:
Observed 2026-11-13 on pull request #4208. A session created a worktree with `make worktree-create`, handed it to a subagent to implement in, and then ran `make pr-open` there itself. It was refused: 'Worktree ... is owned by live session <subagent session> (pid ...); this session is <parent session> ... Refusing BenchBox write preflight: worktree ownership check failed.' The subagent had finished, but subagents share the harness pid, so its claim never goes stale. Recovery was `BENCHBOX_WORKTREE_TAKEOVER=1 make agent-write-preflight`.

`docs/internal/dev-loop-worktrees.md` describes exactly this and says a parent prompt that hands a worktree to a subagent should include the takeover command. But `AGENTS.md` and every page under `docs/agent/` are silent, and `AGENTS.md` tells agents to read `docs/agent/`, not `docs/internal/`. `AGENTS.md` also encourages low-effort subagents for gate runs, which hits the same refusal in the other direction (a subagent sent into the parent's worktree).

Not affected: registered batch members. On 2026-11-13 batch `member-rule-docs` landed and finished two subagent-owned member worktrees with no takeover, because the leader never writes in a member worktree.

Decision gates.
- Choose: (a) document the takeover on an agent-facing page that `AGENTS.md` links; or (b) make the ownership check treat a claim by a finished subagent of the same harness process as released. Prefer (a) unless the check can tell a finished subagent from a live one; if it cannot, (b) would let two live writers into one worktree, which is what the check exists to stop.
- `AGENTS.md` is within about 30 bytes of its instruction budget (agent-instruction-budget-headroom), so the text goes on a linked page.

Guardrails.
- The takeover stays an explicit act: nothing sets `BENCHBOX_WORKTREE_TAKEOVER` by default, in a make target or in a hook.
- The doc says when takeover is legitimate (the other claimant is this session's own finished subagent, or a session confirmed gone) and that it is never used against another live session.
- No change to `scripts/agent_write_preflight.sh` refusal behaviour under option (a).
